newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina judge postpones Liggett papers hearing.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina judge postpones Liggett papers hearing.

text.p: A North Carolina judge put off indefinitely a hearing on his order against Liggett Group distributing internal industry documents believed damaging to other cigarette makers, a court clerk said on Friday.
Superior Court Judge William Freeman imposed a temporary restraining order on Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd., on March 20 and had scheduled a hearing in Forsyth County Court here for Monday.
But the clerk said Freeman will not hold the hearing until an appeal of the order can be heard by a higher court. A date for the appeals court ruling was not immediately known.
The judge's order, ignored by many other judges overseeing anti-tobacco lawsuits outside North Carolina, remained in effect.

Freeman issued his order at the request of Philip Morris Cos. Inc. and other tobacco companies on the same day Liggett agreed to turn over five boxes of papers to state attorneys general to settle legal claims against it.

Excerpts of the papers, described by anti-tobacco lawyers as deeply damaging to the tobacco companies defending themselves against a wide array of legal claims, have been published in newspapers since March 20.
Judges in Texas and other states have ordered Liggett to hand over the papers in pending tobacco cases.
